_description: Fixed hyperparameters of all base models and the stacking meta-learner used by prunestack.
Base models use scikit-learn defaults; only iteration limits are raised to ensure
convergence across the dataset collection. The parameters are identical for every model
in the pool (original model and feature-subset variants); models of one algorithm
differ only in the feature subset they see. No per-dataset tuning is performed.
Reference: Domladovac (2026) - Learning to Prune: Meta-Feature Guided
_notes: An empty object {} means pure scikit-learn defaults.
LogisticRegression / MLP: max_iter raised from 100 / 200 to 1000 (convergence).
HistGradientBoosting: max_iter raised from 100 to 300 boosting iterations.
RandomForestClassifier: n_estimators=100 is the scikit-learn default, stated explicitly.
ElasticNet: max_iter raised from 1000 to 2000 (coordinate descent on correlated features).
random_state is injected at runtime from the experiment seed for every estimator that accepts it.
stacking.<task>.meta_learner: nnls_mlr = multi-response linear regression with non-negative
weights (Ting & Witten, 1999); nnls = non-negative least squares (Breiman, 1996).
random_forest, hist_gradient_boosting. stacking.<task>.params are passed to scikit-learn
based meta-learners and ignored by nnls / nnls_mlr.
